chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Miskan, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man: does anything that passes before him cut off his salat (prayer)? He said: Nothing cuts off the salat (prayer) of a Muslim, but ward off what you can.

key_terms.ادْرَءُوا: ward off or repel, meaning prevent if possible
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِ: the Muslim whose salat (prayer) is being discussed
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat (prayer), meaning the ritual prayer being performed
key_terms.مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ: whatever you are able to do, indicating practical effort within one’s capacity
key_terms.يَقْطَعُ: invalidates or cuts off in the legal sense discussed here

ai.seo_question: Does something passing in front of a person invalidate his salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that things passing in front of a person do not invalidate his salat (prayer). However, one should still try to prevent such interruptions as much as possible, indicating an etiquette of preserving focus and respect in worship.
